description: A single‑file Flask app that serves a modern, realistic 3D car driving game built with Three.js, Tailwind CSS, and Web Audio API, all generated procedurally.
backend_brief: Create a Flask application (variable name app) that defines one route at '/' returning a complete HTML page. The HTML must embed Tailwind CSS via CDN, Three.js (latest stable) via CDN, and all custom JavaScript and CSS inside <script> and <style> tags. No static files or templates are used. The server should run with `python app.py` and listen on the default port (5000). No additional backend logic is required.
frontend_brief:
Inside the single HTML page, implement a full‑screen WebGL canvas powered by Three.js. Build the car, road, environment, trees, buildings, and other props entirely from primitive geometries (BoxGeometry, CylinderGeometry, etc.) and generate textures on‑the‑fly using canvas or procedural shaders. Apply PBR materials (MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhysicalMaterial) with clearcoat, metalness, roughness, and transparency for glass. Set up realistic lighting: directional sun with shadows, hemisphere light, tone mapping (ACESFilmicToneMapping), sRGBEncoding, fog, and a procedural sky gradient. Add a day/night toggle that switches sky color and activates headlights (emissive materials). Implement post‑processing via EffectComposer for bloom and optional vignette.

Physics: Use a lightweight arcade physics approach (custom code) to simulate acceleration, braking, steering, hand‑brake drifting, weight transfer (car body tilt), suspension bounce, and wheel rotation. Update speed, RPM, gear, and distance variables. Detect collisions with obstacles using bounding boxes or raycasting; on impact trigger camera shake, speed penalty, and a thud sound.

Audio: Use the Web Audio API to synthesize an engine sound whose pitch/volume follows RPM, a tire‑screech sound on hand‑brake drift, and a collision thud. Add a horn sound on key press.

Controls: Keyboard – W/A/S/D or arrows for throttle/steering, Space for handbrake, R to reset, H for horn, L for headlights, P to pause, C to cycle camera modes (chase, hood, cockpit, free orbit). Touch UI – on‑screen steering wheel and pedal areas for mobile.

UI/HUD (Tailwind + glassmorphism): Start screen with game title, "Start Driving" button, controls guide, and a colour picker (six preset colours) that updates the car paint live. In‑game overlay with speedometer, RPM bar, gear indicator, distance counter, score/timer, minimap (simple top‑down view of road and nearby objects), and pause menu. Use rounded, blurred cards, neon accents, and smooth transition animations.

Gameplay modes: Free‑roam and Time‑Trial/Score mode. In score mode, award points for distance, near‑misses, and successful drifts. Store the best score in localStorage and display it on the game‑over screen with a restart button.

Performance: Use InstancedMesh for repeated objects (trees, street lamps, traffic cars). Dispose of off‑screen meshes to keep memory low. Adjust camera FOV dynamically for a subtle motion‑blur effect at high speeds.

All scripts, styles, and assets must be embedded; no external files besides CDN links.
